definitions.gloss: to practice; to train; to rehearse
definitions.explanation: To repeat an activity or skill in order to improve at it. Used for practicing musical instruments, sports, languages, and other skills.

examples.japanese: {毎日|まいにち}ピアノを{練習|れんしゅう}している。
examples.english: I practice the piano every day.

examples.japanese: {試合|しあい}に{向|む}けて、チーム{全体|ぜんたい}で{練習|れんしゅう}した。
examples.english: The whole team practiced in preparation for the game.

examples.japanese: {発表|はっぴょう}の{前|まえ}に{何度|なんど}もスピーチを{練習|れんしゅう}したおかげで、{本番|ほんばん}はうまくいった。
examples.english: Thanks to practicing the speech many times before the presentation, the real thing went well.

notes:
One of the most frequently used words for practice and training. Covers a wide range of activities from casual hobbies to serious athletic or artistic training.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {練習|れんしゅう}{試合|しあい}: practice match; scrimmage
- {練習|れんしゅう}{問題|もんだい}: practice problems; exercises
- {練習|れんしゅう}{時間|じかん}: practice time
- {練習|れんしゅう}メニュー: training regimen
- {自主|じしゅ}{練習|れんしゅう}: self-directed practice

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {訓練|くんれん}する: to train — more intensive and systematic; used for military, emergency, or professional training
- {稽古|けいこ}する: to practice — used specifically for traditional arts (martial arts, tea ceremony, dance)
- {特訓|とっくん}する: to do intensive training — implies concentrated, rigorous practice over a short period

USAGE:
The noun {練習|れんしゅう} is very commonly used on its own, often as a compound element. In casual speech, it is sometimes shortened to {練|れん} (e.g., {朝練|あされん} for morning practice).
